global_gates: toolkit parity must describe generic AI tool dialect behavior, not FinRobot syntax
default tests must not import AutoGen, Pandas, provider SDKs, finance providers, q/runtime, or live package implementations
caller and executor roles must remain explicit and separable in tool registration metadata
tool schemas must be declarative JSON-compatible metadata and must not require a provider-specific function-calling API
tool results must be wrapped in a stable envelope with structured success and structured error variants
string and table output adapters must be modeled as dialect adapters rather than Python object behavior

source_concepts: register_toolkits accepts a dict with function/name/description
capabilities.dialect_contract: A tool registry entry may be derived from a callable-like descriptor or from explicit metadata, with canonical name and description fields.
A class-like toolkit can expand into individual tools while preserving an explicit private-member exposure policy.

source_concepts: executor ConversableAgent runs the registered callable
capabilities.dialect_contract: Tool advertisement and tool execution are separate roles connected by a registration edge.

source_concepts: tool config may override name and description
capabilities.dialect_contract: Tool input shape, required fields, description, and capability tags are declarative metadata independent of a provider wire format.

source_concepts: stringify_output returns a string for every successful call
capabilities.dialect_contract: A result envelope carries ok, tool_name, output_format, content, table, artifacts, and provenance fields without exposing provider internals.

source_concepts: register_toolkits raises ValueError for missing or non-callable functions
capabilities.dialect_contract: Registration and execution failures are represented as structured errors with code, message, retryable, stage, and details fields.

source_concepts: stringify_output converts non-table results with str(result)
capabilities.dialect_contract: Scalar and object outputs can be adapted into stable text content while preserving raw output type metadata.
Table-like outputs can expose both a text rendering and a row/column table payload without depending on Pandas.

parity_notes: The source decorator always returns a string on success.
The parity contract keeps that text rendering and also permits structured table payloads.
Callable and dict configurations normalize to the same registry entry.
Invalid function descriptors become structured registration errors.
The code-writing tools are represented as a disabled capability bundle by default.
Local file mutation and code execution remain outside provider-free toolkit parity.
The source spelling is preserved for provenance.
The dialect name normalizes the concept to class toolkit expansion.

caller_responsibilities: advertise tool name, description, schema, and capability tags
executor_responsibilities: run the implementation only when enabled by capability policy
return result envelope or structured error
